headline: Tatum catches fire in second half to sink the Knicks
morning_brew: Friday night at the Garden was a total cardiac event, and I’m still scraping myself off the ceiling. Jayson Tatum decided he wasn't gonna let the Knicks walk out of our building with a win, dropping twenty-five of his thirty-six points in the second half like it was a layup line. It was the kind of takeover that makes you wanna run through a brick wall, and honestly, seeing him put the team on his back after that sluggish start had me feeling like we might just have something special here.

The heavy lifting didn't end with Tatum, though, because the bench finally showed up with a pulse. Neemias Queta was an absolute wrecking ball under the rim with three blocks and double-digit points, and watching him fight for every loose ball made me happier than a fresh Dunks run on a Monday morning. It is only October, but grinding out a win like this against New York feels like a deposit in the Duck Boat fund, even if I have to keep my expectations grounded for another few months.

We aren't done yet because the Bruins are back at the Garden tonight against San Jose. Puck drop is at seven, and my blood pressure needs a break from the high-stakes drama, so I’m looking for a nice, boring blowout victory. I’ll be glued to the couch with my feet up, and if the boys can keep this citywide momentum rolling, I might just have to stop being such a cynical fan for at least forty-eight hours.
